targets.name: FUN_00130270
targets.label: FUN_00130270[gameupd]
targets.reason: Same function as the FUN_00130270 entry above, but on the gate-satisfied snapshot: size=16 / msg[0]=0x010c makes the header self-consistent, so the assert path is skipped and the category-3 packet switch actually dispatches (packet_type 0x19 = client_game_update, the deepest chain). Covers 24.4% vs 10.0% (40/40 PASS) and exercises code the sibling entry never reaches; the sibling still covers the assert/early-exit path, so both are kept. NOTE: both write the same artifacts/equivalence/FUN_00130270_smoke.log, so the log reflects whichever ran last. SKIPs when host snapshot absent.

targets.name: FUN_000d7cd0
targets.reason: Tripwire for the data-page execution guard (hook_code / _mapped_regions). Before it, an indirect call through synthetic state landed in a zero-filled auto-mapped page, whose zeros decode as 2-byte 'add [eax],al' and slid execution through the whole page -- 0% coverage, all 40 seeds ORACLE-CRASH FETCH_UNMAPPED. Now 100.0% coverage, 40/40 PASS, confidence high. Reverting the guard returns this to error.

targets.name: FUN_0005ae70
targets.reason: Sign-extension fix: the squad index is the handle's low word ZERO-extended (original is a plain 'AND ESI,0xffff; PUSH ESI'), but the lift had an (int16_t) cast that sign-extended indices >= 0x8000. Was 32/50 with 'arg[1] to tag_block_get_element: oracle=0x8020 candidate=0xffff8020'; now 50/50 clean. VC71 is blind to it -- 78.4% both before and after -- so this differential is the only guard.

targets.name: event_manager_initialize
targets.reason: Tripwire for the dllimport-indirection seeding (_seed_dllimport_indirection). kb.json HDATA globals are __declspec(dllimport), so the candidate reaches event_manager_globals via a pointer-to-pointer while the delinked oracle references DAT_0046bd40 directly; the unseeded import slot made the candidate pass NULL to csmemset. Was 0/N with 'arg[0]: oracle=0x500000 candidate=0x0'; now clean.

targets.name: player_ui_initialize
targets.reason: Second dllimport-indirection tripwire, different object and global (player_ui_globals @0x46bee0), so the fix is not pinned to one symbol.

targets.name: FUN_00148240
targets.reason: Surface edge-ring 2D point test. The snapshot pins valid surface/edge/vertex tag blocks so the semantic tag_block_get_element stub resolves every lookup; without it 2/40 seeds hit ORACLE-CRASH eip=0x0 on an unrelocated oracle target. Observed 40/40 PASS, 83.6% cov, high confidence. Guards the byte-typed side flag (SETZ BL / MOVZX EDI,BL at 0x1482b9) and the cross-product guard sense at 0x14833c.

targets.name: FUN_00148780
targets.reason: bsp2d surface-reference scan, body-reached path (param_8==0). The snapshot seeds tag_block headers inside the bsp parameter content so the reference matches surface_index and the loop body actually runs: axis selection, sign XOR, t*direction+origin, and both external calls. Observed 30/30 PASS, 75.9% cov, high confidence -- versus 15.4% and weak with no snapshot.

targets.name: FUN_00148780
targets.reason: bsp2d surface-reference scan, no-match path: ref[0] != surface_index so the body is skipped and the loop exhausts to the -1 sentinel. Observed 30/30 PASS, 30.8% cov, moderate. Deliberately NOT registered: the param_8!=0 paths that call the now-ported FUN_00148240. There the candidate runs the real sibling while the oracle stubs it, and the oracle ignores that stub's return entirely -- it yields a constant 0x00400f2c whether the stub is told to return 0 or 1, while the lifted side correctly returns -1 and 7. Oracle-side harness defect, not a lift defect; the call arguments are covered by the stub-arg differential (9 calls, 0 mismatches).
